subject: Clarify fallthrough responsibility for private VPC resilience
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hannah.li@meridiansystems.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify responsibility 'fallthrough' for Meridian private VPC resilience

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for last week's demo — Meridian is seriously considering Redwood Private for our inference tier. Two quick, related questions from our infra team before we move the contract forward:

1) We host the VPC, peering, and edge firewalls in our cloud account. If there is a regional network failure (packet loss between our peering and the Redwood node) that causes higher tail latency or short term unavailability, how does Redwood attribute uptime impact?

2) Our legal team saw a line in the draft SLA about a 'fallthrough' responsibility when customer-managed networking prevents Redwood from delivering traffic to the node. They want the exact trigger and an appeals path clarified — i.e., when will Redwood count that as a customer-side incident vs Redwood-side?

Can you put together a short, non-legal explanation and a proposed appendix we can attach to the SLA? Rajiv (cc'd) is our platform architect and will be the technical reviewer.

Appreciate it —
Hannah
Hannah Li
VP of Engineering, Meridian Systems
Hannah.li@meridiansystems.com

(Attachment: network-diagram-meridian-peg.png)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@meridiansystems.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@meridiansystems.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify responsibility 'fallthrough' for Meridian private VPC resilience

Hi Hannah — great questions. Putting a concise response below and attaching a short draft appendix you can circulate internally.

TL;DR: Redwood attributes incidents to the customer-side when an observable, reproducible network or infra fault exists entirely inside the customer's perimeter (VPC, peering, firewall, on-prem gateway) and our control plane confirms the Redwood service and node were healthy and accepting connections. We treat 'fallthrough' as the operational mode where the request path is blocked or degraded before it reaches our serving runtime.

Key points:
- Evidence gates: attribution will use (a) Redwood side health checks and telemetry, (b) customer-side network traces (tcpdump/flow logs), and (c) BGP/peering status if applicable.
- Measurable thresholds: short-lived packet loss under X% for less than Y minutes gets classified as transient and handled via retries; sustained loss or blackholing that prevents request completion by >Z minutes will be considered a fallthrough incident.
- Appeals: customers can open a review within 5 business days with the joint evidence bundle; Redwood will expedite an attribution review and produce a forensics summary within 3 business days.

I've attached an appendix draft with suggested wording and placeholder thresholds (we can tune these with legal/ops). The draft also lists the exact logs we'll request for evidence (connection logs, node health, peering BGP events).

Next steps: if that looks okay, I can circulate with Neha (security/compliance) and our contracts team to formalize the appendix for the Meridian contract.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
(Attachment: Meridian_SLA_fallthrough_draft_v1.pdf)

Subject: Re: Clarify responsibility 'fallthrough' for Meridian private VPC resilience

Markus — good summary. A few compliance notes from our side: 

1) Evidence retention: for an attribution review we need connection-level metadata and error traces for 30 days. Please confirm Meridian agrees to provide packet captures or VPC flow logs on request (we won't keep captures, just use them for the joint forensics).
2) KMS/Key access: if Meridian elects to use customer-managed keys in their VPC for any traffic-level encryption, we must be explicit that key unavailability or mis-rotation is a customer-side responsibility.
3) Maintenance windows: propose adding a clause that scheduled customer network maintenance (announced 72+ hours in advance in the joint calendar) will be excluded from SLA calculations.

If you want, I can turn these bullets into a clean section for the appendix (e.g., Evidence & Exclusions).

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarify responsibility 'fallthrough' for Meridian private VPC resilience

Hannah — thanks for the fast review. Based on Neha's notes I've updated the appendix with an Evidence & Exclusions section and clearer threshold language. Summary of the changes: 

- Thresholds: defined a 5-minute sustained failure window and a >2% sustained packet loss threshold as the initial 'fallthrough' trigger (placeholders — can tune).
- Evidence & Retention: Redwood will request VPC flow logs, peering BGP dumps, and our node health traces; Meridian to provide captures/flow logs within 3 business days for the first attribution review. Redwood will retain our forensic outputs for 30 days.
- KMS: explicit callout that customer-managed key unavailability is a customer-side exclusion.
- Maintenance: scheduled customer maintenance (72+ hours notice) excluded from SLA calculations; ad-hoc emergency maintenance can be appealed.

I'm attaching Meridian_SLA_fallthrough_draft_v1.pdf (with tracked changes) for review. If Meridian is comfortable with the approach, next steps are: 1) Meridian legal confirms threshold placeholders, 2) Redwood Contracts creates formal appendix, 3) sign & DocuSign.

Would you like me to send the draft to our contracts team now or wait for Meridian legal to confirm thresholds?

Best,
Markus
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

(Attachment: Meridian_SLA_fallthrough_draft_v1.pdf)
